newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha pulled higher by crude but still slopp.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha pulled higher by crude but still slopp.

text.p: NWE naphtha was dragged higher on Monday, although traders said the supply situation in the area remained on the sloppy side, traders said.
IPE Brent futures were 41 cents higher at $18.33 a barrel at 1717 GMT, but naphtha registered only moderate gains.
"It's a bit of a difficult market at the moment," said a broker. "End-users are holding back but there are quite a few sellers."
A Dutch end-user was reported to be offering a Dow spec cargo at $171 cif NWE, but the highest bid received for the parcel was around $168.
Traders noted there were some four to five 10-12,000 tonne cargoes currently available in northwest Europe.
Two players were also reported to be bidding at around $179-$180 for pipeline spec material for May delivery dates.
Traders attributed part of the market's weakness to the sloppy state of the Asian markets where prices continued to be undermined by ample supply.
"In general it's closed," said one trader with regards to the arbitrage.
"Bigger 50-100,000 tonne cargoes may still work if you can get a vessel so stuff is going over where there is the opportunity but we're not seeing a constant stream," said one trader.
One broker noted there was signs that buying interest out of the United States was picking up.
